newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude rises with WTI, diffs flatten.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude rises with WTI, diffs flatten.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose steeply on the heals of increased buying in West Texas Intermediate (WTI) grade midday, while local differentials remained idle.
Diffs for Alaska North Slope (ANS) stood at a $2.20 a barrel discount to December WTI, following the sale of a full cargo on Monday.
BP offered at $1.90 a barrel off December WTI Wednesday, traders said.
Absolute WTI prices jumped 60 cents to $23.95/24.05 as pricier imports prompted traders to buy more domestic oil.
Outright ANS prices moved up 60 cents in line with WTI, hitting $21.65/21.95 a barrel.
Line 63 crude remained thinly traded in typical early month discussion. The grade, like ANS, rose with higher WTI prices to $20.75/21.05 a barrel.
Arco said it moved up the deadline for Line 63 shippers' nominations to late next week or early next.
Wilmington crude was $17.60/$17.70 a barrel, while Kern River crude stayed $16.15/$16.35 a barrel.
